name: Elam
overview: Elam is a male biblical figure noted primarily for his descendants who returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity, highlighting his role in the restoration period of Israel. He is identified as the father of Jehiel and is mentioned in the context of the sealed document in Nehemiah, indicating his family's involvement in the post-exilic community. Though his tribal affiliation is not specified, his lineage reflects continuity within the Jewish remnant.
namesAndTitles: The name Elam means "highland" and is used as a proper name in the Scriptures, appearing notably in Ezra. This meaning may reflect geographical or symbolic significance but is not directly attributed to divine naming in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Elam is recorded as the father of Jehiel, and through him, an ancestor to several other figures such as Athaliah, Mattaniah, Zechariah, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah. He is also considered a descendant of Jacob, situating him within the broader covenantal lineage of Israel. These relationships underline his familial importance in the genealogical records of the post-exilic community.
scriptureSignificance: Elam's significance lies in his connection to the restoration of Judah following captivity, with his sons returning to participate in rebuilding the community and religious life. His inclusion on the sealed document in Nehemiah signifies his family's commitment to the covenant and the reforms undertaken during this period. Thus, Elam represents a link between Israel's past and its renewed future under God's providence.
